episodes.title: Anthropic's Record IPO + What Kevin Got Wrong About the Company in 2023
episodes.about: Anthropic is officially a publicly traded company worth more than a trillion dollars, but some of the people getting rich aren't celebrating. We unpack how employees and early investors are reacting and what the debut tells us about the AI bubble. Then we open up our reporter's notebooks from 2023, when Anthropic was just a 150-person lab with a cramped office, bragging about having "hundreds" of customers. We talk about how this strange company got to this moment and how to feel about the biggest IPO in history going to a company that warns its technology could lead to catastrophe.
episodes.why: Anthropic is now public at over a trillion dollars; Roose and Newton unpack how employees and early investors are reacting, then reopen their 2023 notebooks from when it was a 150-person lab.

episodes.title: The One-Person Biotech | OpenAI Life Sciences
episodes.about: What happens when scientists are no longer limited by human attention? OpenAI's Joy Jiao and Ashoka Rajendra join a16z's Jay Rughani and Jorge Conde to discuss how AI and thousands of parallel agents could reshape drug discovery and development. They trace OpenAI's life sciences work from scientific reasoning to the acquisition of Orchestra Bio, and how agents could search biological data, manage clinical trials, and navigate regulatory and manufacturing workflows. They also discuss AI's role in solving difficult diagnoses and a future where a single person could potentially launch and advance multiple biotech programs.
episodes.why: OpenAI's Joy Jiao and Ashoka Rajendra explain how thousands of parallel agents could search biological data, run trial workflows, and let one person advance multiple biotech programs.

episodes.title: What a Town Full of Vibecoders Says About the Chinese Economy
episodes.about: According to Stanford's AI Index, 84% of people surveyed in China say they are optimistic about AI. In the US, by contrast, 38% of those surveyed say they are optimistic. That's a big gulf in enthusiasm, and you can see it borne out in the stories you read. While in the US we hear about AI doomsday scenarios, in China, you'll hear about grandmas who are obsessed with using OpenClaw. Journalist Afra Wang has spent a lot of time in mainland China reporting from the country's AI hotbed — in a vibecoding-obsessed town outside of Hangzhou; at the for-profit schools where influencers are teaching everyday people how to use the technology; and the content studios that are pumping out AI microdramas.
episodes.why: Journalist Afra Wang reports from a vibecoding-obsessed town outside Hangzhou, for-profit AI schools, and microdrama studios — a ground-level look at why optimism about AI in China runs far ahead of the US.

episodes.title: Why You Should Try Gemini Neon (Even if You Love Fable)
episodes.about: Google's Gemini Neon edged out Fable on a coding benchmark, but its best pitch may be as a second opinion. NLW shares how Neon helped him find the story in an oil episode that Claude and ChatGPT kept turning into a Wikipedia entry, and what happened when he pushed back on its ideas. In the headlines: Anthropic closes its first day of trading up 17%, and Chinese AI labs warn that new U.S. chip restrictions could delay model releases.
episodes.why: Google's Gemini Neon edged out Fable on a coding benchmark; NLW shows where it worked as a second opinion on a story Claude and ChatGPT kept flattening, and where pushing back changed its answers.

episodes.title: Prophet of Doom
episodes.about: The Princeton political historian Gregory Conti has, in his own words, a crusading streak. For a long time, he directed his ire toward left-wing politicization in scholarship and campus culture. But he is now preoccupied with a new concern: what AI will mean for the life of the mind. His prognosis is as grim as it gets. On its current trajectory, he says, AI spells the death of human intellectual striving. That's an apocalyptic vision, but Conti's no street-corner ranter: He's a serious, sober, careful thinker, and anyone concerned with the future of the academy needs to listen.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — Open Questions is the Chronicle of Higher Education's ideas podcast, new to this list; Princeton historian Gregory Conti argues AI on its current trajectory spells the death of human intellectual striving — the episode Dave asked to have added.
